summary.text: 3 of 3 hidden signals for Home Depot have fresh data: 0 tailwinds, 1 headwind, 1 neutral, 1 context. The biggest mover is “Mortgage rates” (+5.0% vs the 4 weeks before). These are clues, not forecasts.

ai.text: Rising mortgage rates suggest a potential headwind for Home Depot, as pricier loans could discourage homeowners from starting new projects. While lumber prices are higher than a year ago, neutral housing starts indicate that new construction activity remains steady. Collectively, these signals hint at a mixed environment for the company.

signals.name: New homes breaking ground
signals.metric: New privately-owned housing units started (annualized, monthly, Census)
signals.what: How many new homes builders started constructing, from the Census Bureau. Every new home needs lumber, fixtures, and appliances.
signals.why: Builders and pros are a big slice of Home Depot's sales, and new homeowners spend heavily on improvements. More starts means more demand down the line.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: New privately-owned housing units started (annualized, monthly, Census): 1.34M/yr pace (last 3 months, average), down 1.9% vs the same period last year. Data through Aug 2026. That's within the ±3% range we treat as normal noise, so it reads as neutral for now.

signals.name: Mortgage rates
signals.metric: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate (Freddie Mac, weekly)
signals.what: The average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage, surveyed weekly by Freddie Mac.
signals.why: People renovate when they buy, sell, or refinance. High mortgage rates freeze the housing market, and with it a lot of big-ticket home projects.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.now: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate (Freddie Mac, weekly): 7.01% (last 4 weeks, average), up 5.0% vs the 4 weeks before. Data through Oct 1, 2026. In plain English: mortgages are getting pricier, which tends to freeze home projects. We read that as a mild headwind for Home Depot.

signals.name: Lumber prices
signals.metric: Producer price index for lumber (monthly, BLS)
signals.what: What lumber mills charge for wood, tracked by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
signals.why: Pricier lumber raises the dollar value of each sale, but it can also price out DIY projects. That is why we treat it as context rather than good or bad.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: Producer price index for lumber (monthly, BLS): 286 (last 3 months, average), up 7.6% vs the same period last year. Data through Aug 2026. In plain English: lumber is pricier than a year ago. For Home Depot the effect cuts both ways, so we show it as context, not a call.
